experience: Sociable scholar with a humiliating secret was easy to inhabit. Motive felt like a dinner conversation; later rounds became a structured evidence elimination exercise. I used written anchors rather than retaining all sixteen names and errands. The answer emerged clearly once method records repeated the key facts.
difficulty_detail: Moderate tracking burden until Method, then a straightforward intersection of salon window, key and linen. Final confidence 96 because all alternate transfer/access routes were explicitly closed.
navigation: Round headings and STOP lines make the sequence clear. Two question pages per round mean some scanning. Host tracking avoids needing to remember who already spoke. Full-page original-detail inspection of pages 07 and 10 included the top white margin, MERIDIAN header, character/round title, Your answer heading and introductory instruction.
question_matching: All transcript questions matched the named group and each prepared answer addressed the question. The self-name in a question group initially looks odd but is usable by someone else. No mismatch experienced.
repetition: Repeated key/no-key and exact entry times are useful for a distracted reader. Identical Opportunity branches add visual bulk without new information. Method preparation records rescue recall but repeated ordinary wipe errands become monotonous across sixteen speakers.
16_present_vs_30_listed: Ignore absent guests is explicit and workable, yet every question page contains names outside the sixteen-person roster. Reed is absent in my arrival task. The substitution instruction prevents blockage, but a host-provided present-guest tick list would reduce scanning and name confusion.
note_space: Page 07 offers three ruled lines under Notes from this round. That is limited for comparing sixteen times and key access. A compact table would help more than prose lines. Method page 10 has no note area. Ballot evidence has only one ruled line, although it requests a three-part proof; usable for a terse summary, cramped for my full reasoning. This assesses rendered layout, not handwriting or physical handling.
memory_load: Names, minutes, key access and later cloth type create substantial working-memory demand. I tracked Tess=trust, Artie=job, Barb=camera first; then narrowed to in-window key users. Prepared transcript review and saved notes were available, so no actual human recall was tested.
